newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close firmer, Pliva to move market.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close firmer, Pliva to move market.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mostly firmer on Friday, led by drugs firm Pliva's third straight record-breaking session and analysts said the stock could continue to move the market upwards in the days ahead.
"Pliva could keep the pace of activity going," said Davor Relja, analyst at Faktor brokerage.
"There are rumours about strong interest of foreign investors for it. Its shares are said to be very much in demand," he said.
There are foreign bidders for other stocks as well, such as food processor Podravka and tourist firms Laguna and Riviera, both from the Istrian town of Porec, he added.

Pliva climbed 15 kuna to fetch 615, setting its third consecutive record this week and selling 1,756 units. Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) rose to $18.55 in London, up from $18.375 on Thursday.
Fifteen of 22 active issues rose on Friday, four fell and three closed flat. But volume shrank to 14,150 from 24,782 units and turnover fell to 6.4 from 11.4 million kuna.

Recent record breaker Zagrebacka Banka's ordinaries led decliners, losing 78 kuna or 3.1 percent to 2,505 on meagre volume of 529 shares. Its GDRs stood at $39.125, unchanged from its all-time London high on Thursday.
Unlike Pliva, Zagrebacka is pausing for a breather, traders said.
"There could be a resting period for Zagrebacka until its half year results are published," said Relja. The results are due in late August or early September.
Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka's ordinary stock was the most actively traded issue with 3,726 shares sold. It inched down one kuna to end at 275.

Traders said the bank could rise on the back of the news that its excellent half-year results exceeded plans for the whole year. But the price of its preference stock, which closed 20 kuna higher at 200, was said to be inflated.
Top gainer was hotelier Arenaturist, rising 25 kuna or 23.8 percent to 130 kuna with 500 shares traded.
Other hoteliers also firmed -- Laguna edged up five kuna to 1,520, Riviera eight to 1,090, Suncani Hvar two to 54 and Istraturist two to 171. Only Jadranturist shed one kuna to 260.
Food processor Podravka added 12 kuna to 287, with 2,594 shares sold.
